comments.author: @MarginFlowTV
comments.text: The reframe that landed for me is that the brands aren't really for guests — they're for property owners. Marriott and Hilton mostly sell a franchise system, a booking engine and a loyalty programme, not rooms. Having thirty brands lets them put a different flag on every building in the same city without cannibalising themselves, and the owner gets to pick the exact price tier and service level. No wonder conversion brands are booming — it's cheaper to reflag an existing hotel than build one. Which brand tier do you think is most overcrowded now?

We think Marriott hotels are very nice and of good quality; however, we have decided to stop staying at them since the owning family made the choice to place copies of the *Book of Mormon* in every hotel room.
